excerpt: Sanctus Georgius, martyr: Patronus caelestis urbis v.d. L dek Zdrój; Suidniciensis, Polonia (8 iun. 2011; Prot. 66/11/L).

summary_en: St George, martyr, is confirmed as heavenly patron of the town of Dzierżoniów (printed 'Dzier oniów' with the 'ż' glyph missing), diocese of Świdnica (Poland); patron of a single town.

celebration.name_latin: Domini nostri Iesu Christi Summi et Aeterni Sacerdotis

summary_en: By decision of Benedict XVI communicated by the Secretariat of State on 14 June 2012, Episcopal Conferences that ask the Congregation may inscribe in their proper calendars the celebration of Our Lord Jesus Christ, Eternal High Priest, with the rank of feast on the Thursday after Pentecost (a movable date); circular letter of the Congregation to the presidents of the Conferences, published with the Latin texts. Recorded at general level because the indult is open to every Conference on request, not an insertion in the General Roman Calendar.
excerpt: mi è gradito comunicarLe che in data 14 giugno 2012 il Signor Cardinale Segretario di Stato (Prot. N. 194.519) mi ha trasmesso la decisione del Santo Padre di concedere alle Conferenze Episcopali, che ne faranno richiesta a questa Congregazione per il Culto Divino e la Disciplina dei Sacramenti, l’iscrizione nei rispettivi Calendari Propri della celebrazione di NOSTRO SIGNORE GESÙ CRISTO SOMMO ED ETERNO SACERDOTE con il grado di festa, il giovedì seguente la solennità di Pentecoste

celebration.name_latin: Domini nostri Iesu Christi Summi et Aeterni Sacerdotis

summary_en: Decree approving and declaring typical the Latin texts of the Mass, Liturgy of the Hours and Roman Martyrology elogium for the feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ, Eternal High Priest (Thursday after Pentecost), prepared for the use of the Episcopal Conferences that request it; the Martyrology entry is printed on p. 368. Recorded because it fixes the Martyrology text of a new feast; the text approval as such is otherwise outside the register.
excerpt: Haec porro Congregatio de Cultu Divino et Disciplina Sacramentorum, vigore peculiarium facultatum ab eodem Summo Pontifice ad hoc tributarum, textum latinum Missae, Liturgiae Horarum et Martyrologii Romani de DOMINO NOSTRO IESU CHRISTO SUMMO ET AETERNO SACERDOTE, prout in adiecto exstat exemplari, libenter probat et typicum esse declarat.

summary_en: Notification of the Congregation (27 January 2016) on the concession of cult when insignes relics of a Blessed (the body, the greater part of it, or the heart) travel outside the places where the Blessed already has legitimate liturgical cult: the Congregation grants ad actum, on request of the pilgrimage's organisers and with the consent of the diocesan bishops concerned, the faculty of liturgical celebrations in the Blessed's honour for the individual churches where the relics are exposed and only for the days they remain there; texts are taken from the approved propers or else from the Common; the Mass and Office of the Blessed are excluded on days nn. 1-5 of the Table of Liturgical Days and permitted with the bishop's consent on days nn. 6-9, with only one Mass of the Blessed on Sundays of Christmas Time and Ordinary Time; the Blessed may be named in the Eucharistic Prayer and the Litany of the Saints. Printed in Latin (pp. 36-37) and Italian (pp. 37-38). A norm on temporary cult rather than a calendar change, so flagged for review.
excerpt:
Prot. N. 717/15
NOTIFICATIO DE CULTUS CONCESSIONE QUANDO INSIGNES BEATORUM RELIQUIAE PEREGRINANTUR
Quando insignes Beati reliquiae peregrinantur (id est corpus, maior corporis pars, cor), facultas ritus liturgicos celebrandi in eius honore conceditur a Congregatione de Cultu Divino et Disciplina Sacramentorum pro singulis ecclesiis ubi illae reliquiae ad fidelium venerationem exponentur, et pro diebus in quibus eaedem ibi aderunt.

summary_en: By decree Laetitiae plena, at the mandate of Pope Francis, the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, is inscribed in the General Roman Calendar on the Monday after Pentecost, to be celebrated every year as an obligatory memorial in every Calendar and liturgical book of the Roman Rite; where by approved particular law it is already celebrated on a different day at a higher rank, that may continue. The Latin decree (pp. 52-54) is followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 54-69) and by the annexed additions to the Calendar, Missal, Ordo lectionum, Liturgy of the Hours and Martyrology (pp. 70-76, including the new elogium 10bis among the mobile celebrations of the Martyrologium Romanum).
excerpt: Summus autem Pontifex Franciscus, cum perpendisset quantum hæc fovenda devotio ad Pastorum, religiosorum, christifidelium Ecclesiæ sensum maternum ac genuinam marialem pietatem, adhuc proficere possit, decrevit memoriam B. Mariæ Virginis, Ecclesiæ Matris, in Calendarium Romanum inscribendam esse Feria II post Pentecosten et quotannis celebrandam.

summary_en: Notification on the new memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church (Monday after Pentecost): the Missal rubric allowing the Pentecost Mass or a Mass of the Holy Spirit on the Monday and Tuesday after Pentecost remains in force but does not alter precedence, which is governed solely by the Table of Liturgical Days; all else being equal the obligatory memorial is to be preferred; its readings (Ordo lectionum Missae n. 572 bis) are to be treated as proper and used in place of the weekday readings; and when the memorial coincides with another memorial of a Saint or Blessed, the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary prevails (as the Immaculate Heart is linked to the Sacred Heart, so this memorial is linked to Pentecost). Printed in Latin, English, Spanish and Italian (pp. 80-86). Flagged for review because it is a precedence rule rather than a calendar change.
excerpt: Cum autem memoria B.M.V. Ecclesiæ Matris sit Pentecoste coniuncta, sicut pariter memoria Immaculati Cordis B.M.V. celebrationi Sacratissimi Cordis Iesu coniuncta est, in casu occurrentiæ cum alia memoria alicuius Sancti vel Beati, iuxta liturgicam traditionem præstantiæ inter personas, memoria B.M.V. prævalere debet.

summary_en: One-year ruling for the year 2022 only (Responsum ad dubia de Calendario liturgico exarando pro anno 2022, 11 May 2020, no protocol number printed): (a) Mary Mother of God, Saturday 1 January, and the Second Sunday after the Nativity, 2 January: on 1 January II Vespers and the evening Mass are of the solemnity; (b) St Joseph, Saturday 19 March, and the Third Sunday of Lent, 20 March: on 19 March I Vespers and the evening Mass are of the Sunday; (c) the Nativity of St John the Baptist and the Sacred Heart both falling on Friday 24 June: the Sacred Heart is celebrated on 24 June and the Nativity of St John the Baptist is transferred to Thursday 23 June with its II Vespers omitted and I Vespers of the Sacred Heart celebrated, but where St John the Baptist is patron of the nation, diocese, city or religious community, his Nativity is kept on Friday 24 June and the Sacred Heart is transferred to Thursday 23 June up to and including None; (d) Twentieth Sunday in Ordinary Time, 14 August, and the Assumption, Monday 15 August: on 14 August I Vespers and the Vigil Mass of the Assumption are celebrated.
excerpt: Sollemnitas Nativitatis S. Ioannis Baptistæ et sollemnitas Sacratissimi Cordis Iesu, eadem die 24 iunii coincidentes. – Die 24 iunii, feria VI: sollemnitas Sacratissimi Cordis Iesu celebretur. Sollemnitas Nativitatis S. Ioannis Baptistae ad diem 23 iunii, feriam V, transferatur, II Vesperæ omittantur.

summary_en: By decree Misericordia eius, at the mandate of Pope Francis, the name of Saint Maria Faustina (Helena) Kowalska, virgin, is inscribed in the General Roman Calendar and her optional memorial is to be celebrated by all on 5 October; the new memorial is to be inserted in every Calendar and liturgical book for Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours. The Latin decree (pp. 89-90) is followed by English, French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 91-96) and by the annexed additions to the Calendar, Missal, Ordo lectionum, Liturgy of the Hours and Martyrology (pp. 97-101, including a new elogium in first place on 5 October).
excerpt: decrevit, ut nomen sanctæ Mariæ Faustinæ (Helenæ) Kowalska, virginis, in Calendario Romano generali inscriberetur et eius memoria ad libitum quotannis die 5 mensis Octobris ab omnibus celebraretur.

summary_en: By decree of 25 January 2021, at the mandate of Pope Francis, three optional memorials are inscribed in the General Roman Calendar: St Gregory of Narek, abbot and Doctor of the Church, on 27 February; St John De Avila, priest and Doctor of the Church, on 10 May; St Hildegard of Bingen, virgin and Doctor of the Church, on 17 September. The new memorials are to be inserted in every Calendar and liturgical book for Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours; the Latin decree (p. 122) is followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 123-127) and by the annexed 'Additiones in libris liturgicis' (pp. 128-135: Calendar, Missal collects, Ordo lectionum nn. 536bis, 561bis, 641bis, Liturgy of the Hours, and new Martyrology elogia to be added in first place on 27 February and 10 May and in second place on 17 September). The Nota circa i testi liturgici (Prot. 35/21-40/21, pp. 146-151) confirms that in the Martyrologium Romanum the elogia of these saints, now carrying the title of Doctor, take those places. The decree's own Latin text (p. 122) has no printed page number.
excerpt: Summus Pontifex FRANCISCUS in Calendarium Romanum generale inseri decrevit subsequentes celebrationes, gradu memoriæ ad libitum: sancti Gregorii Narecensis, abbatis et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 27 mensis Februarii, sancti Ioannis De Avila, presbyteri et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 10 mensis Maii, sanctæ Hildegardis Bingensis, virginis et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 17 mensis Septembris.

summary_en: By decree of 26 January 2021, at the mandate of Pope Francis, the memorial of 29 July in the General Roman Calendar, hitherto of St Martha alone, becomes the memorial of Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus; the memorial is to appear under this title in all Calendars and liturgical books for Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours. Latin decree (p. 136) followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 136-141) and by the annexed 'Variationes et additiones' (pp. 142-145: Calendar entry '29 Ss. Marthæ, Mariæ et Lazari, Memoria', Missal formulary with new collect, Ordo lectionum n. 607, Liturgy of the Hours, and a new Martyrology elogium replacing the first elogium of 29 July, with elogium n. 2 omitted; the Nota, pp. 146-151, lists which texts are new). The API keeps the 1970 Missal key StMartha for this memorial.
excerpt: Summus Pontifex FRANCISCUS, annuens huius Dicasterii propositis, disposuit ut memoria sanctorum Marthæ, Mariæ et Lazari in Calendario Romano generali die 29 iulii inscriberetur. Hac denominatione memoria igitur ista cunctis Calendariis et Libris liturgicis pro Missæ et Liturgiæ Horarum celebratione indicanda erit

summary_en: General executive decree 'Postquam Summus Pontifex' implementing can. 838 CIC after the motu proprio Magnum Principium (approved by Pope Francis, dated 22 October 2021). Its section 'De Dioecesium et Familiarum Religiosarum propriis' (nn. 50-55) restates that dioceses, institutes of consecrated life, societies of apostolic life and others with the right have their own particular Calendar, Proper of Masses and of the Liturgy of the Hours and Martyrology; that proper celebrations are inserted harmoniously into the General Roman Calendar, the diocesan calendar taking account of national and regional calendars; that every particular Calendar drawn up by the competent authority must be approved by the Apostolic See, the competent authority (bishop, superior or superior general) requesting the 'recognitio' of the Calendar and Proper from the Congregation with a report on the reasons for each variation or inscription of celebrations. Part II 'Variationes' (pp. 215-222) amends the praenotanda of the liturgical books accordingly, including Martyrologium Romanum praenotanda nn. 38 and 41 on the Proprium Martyrologii. Latin text pp. 152-161, followed by Italian, English, French, German and Spanish versions (pp. 162-214). Flagged for review: a procedural norm on particular calendars rather than an act naming a calendar or celebration.
excerpt: 51. Celebrationes propriae in Calendarium Romanum generale congruenter inseruntur. Calendarium liturgicum dioecesanum prae oculis Calendarium nationale et regionale habere oportet. Omnia Calendaria particularia, a competenti auctoritate confecta, ab Apostolica Sede approbari debent.

The date is printed "4 aug. 2107", evidently a misprint for 2017, transcribed as printed; this act restores holy days of obligation to their proper days.
excerpt: Angliae et Cambriae: sollemnitates in Ascensione Domini et in Epiphania Domini diebus illis propriis assignantur, scilicet quadragesima post Pascha et 6 ianuarii. Si vero sollemnitas in Epiphania Domini in sabbato occurrat sequenti diei dominicae assignetur; si vero in feria secunda dominicae praecedenti (4 aug. 2107; Prot. 180/17).

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' (nn. 5-8), unofficial responses of the Congregation: Holy Family and Baptism of the Lord have I Vespers (the printed 'Negative' in the answer to n. 5 is struck through by hand on the page); the Mass of the II Sunday after Christmas is that of the new Missal; with the Vigil of Ascension abolished the Mass is of the preceding Sunday and the Office for 1970 as in the Breviary; and, for regions transferring Epiphany, Ascension and Corpus Christi to Sunday, a day-by-day calendar for 4-12 January, 6-10 May and 28-31 May 1970. The page states these solutions have orientative, not official, value.
excerpt: 8. Quomodo ordinanda est celebratio Missae et Officii divini in regionibus ubi sollemnitates Epiphaniae et Ascensionis Domini ac Corporis Christi in dominicam transferuntur? Resp.: Attenta declaratione anno praeterito facta a Sacra Congregatione Rituum (Cf. Notitiae, vol. IV, 1968, p. 279), adveniente anno 1970, ubi supradictae sollemnitates in dominicam transferuntur, celebrentur secundum Calendarium quod sequitur

summary_en: Corrigenda to the printed volume Calendarium Romanum (1969): 'Ss.mae Eucharistiae' in Normae n. 7 is to read 'SS.mi Corporis Christi'; the apposition 'presbyteri' is to be deleted after the names of S. Paulus Miki and S. Hieronymus Emiliani; further corrections to the historical commentary (list of saints removed from the Calendar, place of death of S. Romuald, year of death of S. Maria Goretti, place of death of S. John Capistran, memorial of Ss. Bacchus and Apuleius, geographical index). No protocol or date is printed; the same Hieronymus Emiliani correction appears as a footnote on p. 178 of the Calendar in Notitiae 46.
excerpt: In volumine Calendarium Romanum (Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis 1969), quaedam menda irrepserunt, quae corrigenda sunt uti sequitur: p. 12, n. 7: loco Ss.mae Eucharistiae: SS.mi Corporis Christi p. 24, 41, 164: post nomen S. Pauli Miki, tollatur appositio presbyteri. p. 24, 45, 170: item post nomen S. Hieronymi Emiliani, tollatur appositio presbyteri.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' (nn. 16-21), unofficial responses: the anniversary of dedication and the solemnity of the principal patron of the place or of the title of one's own church may be transferred to a Sunday per annum or of Christmastide but not to Sundays of Advent, Lent or Easter or Sundays with a general solemnity (and not for the cathedral, a regional or national patron or a secondary patron); church titles are not to be changed even when the saint is no longer in the general Calendar; no commemoration of the weekday on solemnities in Advent and Lent; Rogations and Ember Days follow the episcopal conference or bishop; no vigil Mass of Christmas on the morning of 24 December.
excerpt: 16. Utrum anniversarium Dedicationis ecclesiae et sollemnitas patroni aut tituli ecclesiae in dominicam transferri possint? Resp.: Affirmative, si agitur de dominica per annum vel temporis Nativitatis et de anniversario Dedicationis ecclesiae propriae vel de patrono principali loci aut de titulo ecclesiae propriae, quae celebrantur tanquam sollemnitates.

summary_en: Variations introduced into the 'Normae universales de Anno liturgico et de Calendario' with the editio typica of the Missale Romanum: n. 13 (feasts of the Lord falling on Sundays per annum and of Christmas time have First Vespers), n. 56 b-d (assignment of saints' celebrations to the dies natalis, and transfer of impeded celebrations in general or particular calendars), n. 59, 5 (feasts of the Lord inscribed in the General Calendar) and n. 60 (impeded solemnities transferred to the nearest free day). No protocol or date is printed on the page; the Missal was promulgated by the decree Prot. n. 166/70 of 26 March 1970 (Notitiae 54, p. 169).
excerpt:
VARIATIONES IN « CALENDARIUM ROMANUM » INDUCTAE (Litteris italicis inscribuntur verba addita vel mutata)
I. NORMAE UNIVERSALES DE ANNO LITURGICO ET DE CALENDARIO
n. 13 « Festa intra fines diei naturalis celebrantur; proinde non habent I Vesperas, nisi de festis Domini agatur quae in dominicis « per annum » et temporis Nativitatis occurrunt et pro earum Officio substituuntur ».

summary_en: General Roman Calendar (editio typica of the Missale Romanum, 1970): the words 'et Sanguinis' are added to the title of the solemnity of the Most Holy Body of Christ, which becomes 'SS.mi Corporis et Sanguinis Christi'. No protocol or date is printed on the page; the Missal was promulgated by the decree Prot. n. 166/70 of 26 March 1970 (Notitiae 54, p. 169).
excerpt:
II. CALENDARIUM ROMANUM GENERALE
Nulla immutatio sed tantummodo addita sunt verba « et Sanguinis » titulo sollemnitatis « SS.mi Corporis Christi »

summary_en: General Roman Calendar (editio typica of the Missale Romanum, 1970): the memorials of St Cajetan and St Dominic in August are swapped by agreement between the Dominicans and the Clerics Regular: 7 August now carries Ss. Sixtus II and companions and St Cajetan (optional memorials), 8 August St Dominic (memorial). The plenary-session report on p. 226 prints the same change as '(7-8 iulii)', evidently for augusti. No protocol or date is printed on the page; the Missal was promulgated by the decree Prot. n. 166/70 of 26 March 1970 (Notitiae 54, p. 169).
excerpt:
et levis translatio facta est in festis S. Caietani et S. Dominici, conventione facta inter familias religiosas Dominicanorum et Clericorum Regularium, et a Sancta Sede accepta ob rationes pastorales.
Augustus: 4 S. Ioannis Mariae Vianney, presbyteri Memoria / 5 In Dedicatione basilicae S. Mariae / 6 IN TRANSFIGURATIONE DOMINI Festum / 7 Ss. Xysti II, papae, et sociorum, martyrum / S. Caietani, presbyteri / 8 S. Dominici, presbyteri Memoria

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' n. 44: an official reply on how impeded solemnities are transferred. In general to the nearest free day (Normae n. 60); but solemnities falling on Sundays of Advent and Lent (e.g. St Joseph or the Annunciation on Passion/Palm Sunday) are, by n. 5 of the Normae, celebrated on the preceding Saturday; if that Saturday is not free of celebrations under nn. 1-8 of the table of precedence, the general principle of n. 60 applies. No protocol or date is printed.
excerpt:
44. Quomodo transferendae sunt sollemnitates quae impediuntur a die liturgico qui praecedentia gaudet?
Generatim sollemnitates, quae impediuntur, ad proximiorem diem transferuntur (cf. Normae de Anno liturgico et de Calendario n. 60). [...] n. 5 supradictarum Normarum statuit ut in his temporibus sollemnitates forte die dominica occurrentes, sabbato praecedenti, de more, celebrentur.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'De celebratione annuali Dedicationis ecclesiae' (no protocol or date printed), announcing the norms of the forthcoming Ordo dedicationis ecclesiae: the anniversary of the dedication of the cathedral is kept with the grade of solemnity in the cathedral itself and of feast in every other church of the diocese, on the day the church was consecrated, and is assigned to the nearest free day when that day is perpetually impeded; the anniversary of a church's own dedication is a solemnity whose day the local community chooses once for all with the bishop's approval - the anniversary of the consecration, the nearest Sunday in Ordinary Time, or the Sunday before All Saints - and where the day of dedication is unknown it is the Sunday before All Saints or 25 October.
excerpt: Celebratio anniversaria Dedicationis ecclesiae cathedralis peragenda est, gradu sollemnitatis, in ipsa ecclesia cathedrali, gradu autem festi, aliis in ecclesiis dioecesis, recurrenti die, quo consecrata est ecclesia. Quando haec dies perpetuo impeditur, tunc celebratio assignatur proximiori diei, qui sit liber.

summary_en: Grants that the celebration of Blessed Paula Frassinetti may be held on 12 June in the Congregation of the Sisters « Dorotee » (Sisters of St Dorothy); the Summarium line prints neither a date nor a protocol number, so both are null and the id is page-based.
excerpt: Congregatio Sororum, v. d. « Dorotee »: conceditur ut celebratio Beatae Paolae Frassinetti peragi valeat die 12 iunii.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'De calendariis particularibus' (no protocol or date printed), on which calendar religious who have a proper calendar follow: celebrating alone they may keep either their proper calendar or that of the local church; in choir or in common the proper calendar is always kept, except that the Congregation has granted some religious families the diocesan calendar with their own celebrations added; and where a proper calendar differs from the region's or the nation's in proper days or in the grade of certain celebrations, religious should adapt theirs to the national or regional calendar, and are bound to do so in celebrations with the people. Religious are in any case bound to keep the anniversary of the dedication of the cathedral of the diocese where they live and the principal patrons of the place and of the wider territory.
excerpt: Utrum religiosi, qui calendarium proprium habent, Missam et Liturgiam Horarum celebrare possint iuxta calendarium ecclesiae localis, dioecesis, regionis vel nationis in quibus degunt? Resp.: Normas a diversis libris liturgicis datas hac de re in mentem revocare oportet.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'De dedicatione ecclesiae' (no protocol or date printed): the anniversary of the dedication of a concathedral is NOT celebrated throughout the diocese but only in that church, since the cathedral alone is the sign of the unity of the local Church and only its dedication anniversary is kept by the whole diocese - with the grade of solemnity in the cathedral and of feast in the other churches. Where a diocese was formed by uniting several dioceses that still keep some unity of their own (their own curia and chapter), each of them may keep the anniversary of its own cathedral.
excerpt: An celebrandum sit in tota dioecesi anniversarium dedicationis Ecclesiae concathedralis. Resp.: Negative. ... Quando autem in dioecesi concathedralia habentur anniversarium earum Dedicationis peragitur tantum in ipsa ecclesia dedicata, minime vero in dioecesi.

target.institute: Sorores Dominicanae (Conventus Corporis Christi, Menlo Park)

summary_en: In the Dominican Sisters' convent of Corpus Christi at Menlo Park (U.S.A.) the memorial of Our Lady of the Rosary may be celebrated every year on 7 October even when it falls on a Sunday in Ordinary Time; a single-convent concession. The date is printed as « 5 sept. » with no year (the Summarium covers 16 Jul 1973 - 15 Jan 1974), so date is null.
excerpt: Sorores Dominicanae, 5 sept. (Prot. n. 1243/73): conceditur ut in Conventu corporis Christi, loci v.d. « Menlo Park » (U.S.A.), quotannis celebrari valeat die 7 octobris memoria B. Mariae Virginis a Rosario, etiam cum eadem die, dominica temporis « per annum » occurrit.

summary_en: One-year rulings for 1975 (Documentorum explanatio « De calendario liturgico anni 1975 », no protocol or date): because 25 March 1975 falls on Tuesday of Holy Week, the solemnity of the Annunciation is celebrated on 7 April 1975, Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter (Normae n. 60); the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed is kept on Sunday 2 November 1975 at Mass (the Liturgy of the Hours is of the Sunday); and on Sundays 14 September and 9 November 1975 the Exaltation of the Holy Cross and the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica are celebrated.
excerpt: DE CALENDARIO LITURGICO ANNI 1975. 1. Quando celebranda erit sollemnitas Annuntiationis Domini? R. Cum anno 1975, die 25 martii incidat feria III Hebdomadae Sanctae, iuxta tabulam dierum liturgicorum secundum ordinem praecedentiae dispositam et n. 60 Normarum de anno liturgico et de calendario, sollemnitas Annuntiationis Domini celebrabitur die 7 aprilis, feria II post dominicam in Albis.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'De Missa diei dominicae et festi de praecepto vespere diei praecedentis anticipata' (no protocol or date printed), on the case the general norm does not settle: when a solemnity of precept falls on a Saturday or a Monday, the evening of the first day belongs to two liturgical days at once. The Congregation gives four indications: the general principle stays Eucharisticum mysterium n. 28; where a Sunday and a solemnity concur the integrity of the whole liturgical day is better kept by applying to the evening Mass the rule given for Vespers (Normae universales n. 61); on the vigils of the solemnities that have a proper Vigil Mass - Christmas, the Nativity of John the Baptist, Ss Peter and Paul, the Assumption - that Vigil Mass is said even when the day falls on a Sunday; and the local Ordinary indicates the practice to be followed at the start of the year in the diocese's own liturgical calendar, even derogating from the above where pastoral reasons make one of the two Masses preferable.
excerpt: 3. In Vigilia sollemnitatum in quibus peculiaris Missa vigiliae habetur (Nativitas Domini, Nativitas S. Ioannis Baptistae, SS. Petrus et Paulus, Assumptio B. Mariae V.), haec dicatur etiamsi die dominica incidat.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' (no protocol or date printed): the anniversary of the dedication of the cathedral may NOT be kept on a Sunday in Ordinary Time. It is a particular feast of the Lord celebrated throughout the diocese, and in the Table of Liturgical Days only feasts of the Lord inscribed in the General Calendar (n. 5) take precedence over those Sundays, not proper feasts (n. 8b). Where the bishop wishes to gather the whole diocese on a Sunday, he may instead use the faculty of IGMR n. 332 for a Mass answering a graver need or pastoral advantage.
excerpt: Utrum anniversarium Dedicationis ecclesiae cathedralis celebrari possit in dominica temporis « per annum ». R. Negative. Nam agitur de festo Domini particulari in tota dioecesi celebrando (cf. Normae de Calendario, n. 52 a, c).

summary_en: One-year ruling for 1975: since the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed falls on Sunday 2 November 1975, the Congregation states that the evening Mass of 1 November is that of the solemnity of All Saints, the liturgical day of higher rank; communiqué published in L'Osservatore Romano of 29 October 1975, no protocol or decree date printed.
excerpt: Da varie parti si domanda quale Messa debba essere celebrata la sera del 1º novembre. ... Perciò in questo caso, la Messa celebrata il 1° novembre sera sarà della solennità di Tutti i Santi (cf. « Tabula dierum liturgicorum », 1, 3: « Missale Romanum », p. 110).

summary_en: List of the proper days of celebration of those beatified or canonized during the Holy Year 1975 - Beati: Maria Eugenia Milleret de Brou 10 March; Caesar de Bus 15 April; Carolus Steeb 15 December; Carolus Joseph Eugenius de Mazenod 21 May; Arnoldus Janssen 15 January; Ioseph Freinademetz 28 January; Maria Teresia Ledóchowska 6 July; Ezechiel Moreno Diaz 19 August; Gaspar Bertoni 12 June; Vincentius Grossi 7 November; Ioanna Francisca Michelotti 1 February; Maria Droste zu Vischering 8 June; Ioseph Moscati 12 April - Sancti: Ioannes Baptista a Conceptione 14 February; Vincentia Maria Lopez y Vicuña 26 December; Elisabeth Anna Bayley Seton 4 January; Ioannes Macias 16 September; Oliverius Plunkett 1 July; Iustinus de Jacobis 31 July; no protocol or date printed.
excerpt: De die proprio celebrationis Sanctorum vel Beatorum qui durante Anno Sancto 1975 Beatificati vel Canonizati sunt.

summary_en: The Daughters of St Camillus may celebrate St Camillus de Lellis on 14 July with the rank of solemnity and the Blessed Virgin Mary 'Salus infirmorum' on 16 November with the rank of feast; the line prints neither a date nor a protocol number.
excerpt: « Istituto Figlie di S. Camillo »: conceditur ut celebratio S. Camilli de Lellis die 14 iulii gradu sollemnitatis atque celebratio BMV sub titulo « Salus infirmorum » die 16 nov. gradu festi peragi valeant.

summary_en: Response to a dubium (Dubia section, no protocol or date printed) ruling that where particular calendars assign the celebration of the B.V.M. Queen of Apostles to the Saturday after the Ascension, it is kept on the Saturday after the Sixth Sunday of Easter where the Ascension is on Thursday, and on the Saturday after the Seventh Sunday of Easter where the Ascension is transferred to that Sunday. Recorded as kind other because it is an interpretative response affecting the date of a celebration in particular calendars, not a decree; the page prints no page number (52 taken from the table of contents).
excerpt: R. In locis in quibus habetur celebratio B.M.V. Reginae Apostolorum, eadem celebratio sabbato quod sequitur Ascensionem Domini, peragi debet, scilicet: a) Sabbato post dominicam VI Paschae, in locis in quibus Ascensio Domini feria V eiusdem hebdomadae celebratur; b) Sabbato post dominicam VII Paschae, in locis in quibus Ascensio Domini dominicae VII Paschae assignatur.

celebration.name_latin: Ss. Ioannes Fisher, episcopus, et Thomas Morus, martyres; S. Paulinus, episcopus

summary_en: Corrigendum (Varia, no protocol or date of its own) on the O.S.B. proper calendar for 22 June: the calendar printed in the Thesaurus Liturgiae Horarum monasticae (1977, confirmed 10 February 1977, Prot. CD 1415/76) shows only the optional memorial of Sts John Fisher and Thomas More, while the calendar in the Proprium Missarum ad usum Confoederationis O.S.B. (1975) shows the optional memorial of St Paulinus; the Congregation rules that the calendar printed in the Proprium Missarum, confirmed 22 June 1972 (Prot. n. 829/72), must be followed, the mention of St Paulinus of Nola having been dropped from the Thesaurus by a typographical accident. The opening page prints no page number (499 taken from the table of contents). Marked for review: a clarification rather than a decree.
excerpt: B. Calendarium proprium O.S.B. — Die 22 iunii, Calendarium O.S.B., quod invenitur in Thesauro Liturgiae Horarum monasticae, Romae 1977, p. 31 [...] veluti memoriam ad libitum illam indicat Ss. Ioannis Fisher, episcopi, et Thomae More, martyrum. E contra, Calendarium quod invenitur in capite Proprii Missarum ad usum Confoederationis O.S.B., Romae, 1975, p. 7, eodem die 22 iunii memoriam alteram ad libitum indicat: S. Paulini, episcopi. Quodnam Calendarium sequendum? R. Evidens est quod servari debent indicationes Calendarii publici iuris facti in capite Proprii Missarum, pp. 5-11, iuxta confirmationem a Sacra Congregatione pro Cultu Divino datam (Prot. n. 829/72 diei 22 iunii 1972).

summary_en: Clarification published by the Congregation (Varia, signed A. D.) on the occasion of the 15th centenary of St Benedict: as principal patron of Europe proclaimed by Paul VI on 24 October 1964 with all the liturgical honours of principal patrons of places, St Benedict (11 July) must be celebrated in the countries of Europe with the grade of feast under Table of Liturgical Days n. 8c, not merely as the obligatory memorial of the General Calendar. Marked for review: an editorial responsum with no protocol number or date, not a decree.
excerpt: Il est exact que, selon la Tabula dierum liturgicorum citée ci-dessus, le patron d'une nation, ou même celui d'un territoire plus vaste comme une confédération ou un ensemble de nations, est célébré avec le degré liturgique de festum. Cette norme doit s'appliquer à S. Benoît, depuis que Paul VI, en proclamant celui-ci Patron de l'Europe, le 24 octobre 1964, a déclaré formellement (A.A.S. 56/1964, pp. 966-967)

summary_en: Not a decree: the report of the US Bishops' Committee on the Liturgy (meeting of 15 June 1982) records the Committee's recommendation to add Blessed André Bessette and Blessed Marie-Rose Durocher to the Proper Calendar for the Dioceses of the USA and to transfer the memorial of Blessed Kateri Tekakwitha from 17 April to another date; the NCCB was to vote on « three requested changes/additions to the Proper Calendar » in November 1982. Recorded for review as a pending national-calendar change without protocol or Congregation act.
excerpt: Acting on a number of requests sent to the Committee, the members decided to recommend the addition of Blessed André Bessette and Blessed Marie-Rose Durocher to the Proper Calendar for the Dioceses of the USA; and the transfer of the memorial of Blessed Kateri Tekakwitha from April 17 to another more suitable date.

summary_en: One-year ruling for the year 1984 on occurrences in the General Calendar: on 8 January (Epiphany transferred to Sunday) the Baptism of the Lord moves to Monday 9 January; on 25 March the Annunciation is anticipated to Saturday 24 March because of the Third Sunday of Lent; on 24 June (Corpus Christi on Sunday) the Nativity of St John the Baptist is transferred to the nearest free day (23 or 25 June) chosen by the Conference or the local bishop; on Friday 29 June the Sacred Heart is transferred to 28 or 30 June, or, where Sts Peter and Paul is not of precept, the Sacred Heart is kept on 29 June and the Apostles are transferred.
excerpt:
DE CALENDARIO LITURGICO EXARANDO PRO ANNO 1984
Redactores nonnulli « Ordinis Missae celebrandae et Officii divini persolvendi » dubium proposuerunt de Calendario liturgico exarando pro venturo anno 1984, ob occurrentiam celebrationum, quae sequuntur:

summary_en: Response of the Congregation « De Calendario liturgico exarando pro anno 1984-1985 »: a one-year ruling for the liturgical year 1984-1985 on which Mass and Vespers are used on the evening of a Saturday or Sunday when a solemnity or feast falls next to a Sunday (8-9 Dec 1984 Immaculate Conception / Advent II; 2-3 Feb 1985 Presentation / Sunday IV; 23-24 June Sunday XII / Nativity of St John the Baptist; 29-30 June Sts Peter and Paul / Sunday XIII; 14-15 Sept Exaltation of the Cross / Sunday XXIV; 2-3 Nov All Souls / Sunday XXXI; 9-10 Nov Dedication of the Lateran / Sunday XXXIII): the Mass satisfying the precept has precedence, and for the Office n. 61 of the Normae universales is kept with a possible derogation in celebrations with the people; episcopal conferences and diocesan bishops may indicate the practice in their particular calendars. No protocol number or date is printed.
excerpt: DE CALENDARIO LITURGICO EXARANDO PRO ANNO 1984-1985. Redactores nonnulli « Ordinis Missae celebrandae et Officii Divini persolvendi » dubia proposuerunt de Calendario liturgico pro anno Domini 1984-1985, quae respiciunt formularia Missae et Vesperarum horis vespertinis sabbati vel dominicae adhibenda, quando sollemnitas quaedam, de praecepto servanda vel non, die sabbati aut feria secunda occurrit.

celebration.name_latin: Sancti Cyrillus, monachus, et Methodius, episcopus

summary_en: Publication (no protocol, no date) of a new Latin Mass text for Sts Cyril, monk, and Methodius, bishop, patrons of Europe, with the statement that their celebration is kept on 14 February as a feast in all the dioceses of Europe, following the apostolic letter Egregiae virtutis of 31 December 1980; recorded as a text publication restating the wider-region grade, not as a new decree.
excerpt: Publici iuris hic facimus novum textum, lingua latina exaratum, Missae Sanctorum Patronorum, in omnibus Europae dioecesibus quotannis die 14 februarii gradu festi celebrandae.

summary_en: One-year ruling for 1989 only: because the solemnity of St Joseph (19 March) coincides with Palm Sunday in 1989, it is anticipated to Saturday 18 March in accordance with n. 60 of the General Norms; where it is not a holy day of obligation the Bishops' Conference may transfer it to another day outside Lent (n. 56). Printed as a notice of the Congregation signed by the Secretary, without protocol number or date.
excerpt: Anno 1989 habebitur occurrentia sollemnitatis S. Ioseph (die 19 martii) cum Dominica in Palmis de Passione Domini et sollemnitatis Annuntiationis Domini (die 25 martii) cum Sabbato Sancto. [...] Iuxta n. 60 Normarum universalium de anno liturgico et de calendario, sollemnitas S. Ioseph anticipatur sabbato die 18 martii.

summary_en: Ruling for 1989 with a standing rule: in 1989 the solemnity of the Annunciation (25 March, Holy Saturday) is celebrated on Monday 3 April, after the Second Sunday of Easter; and from then on, whenever the Annunciation falls on a day of Holy Week, it is always to be transferred to the Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter. Printed as a notice of the Congregation without protocol number or date.
excerpt: Sollemnitas Annuntiationis Domini celebranda erit die 3 aprilis, feria II post Dominicam II Paschae. Ab illa vice ac deinceps ipsa sollemnitas, quotiescumque occurrit aliquo die Maioris Hebdomadae, semper ad feriam II post Dominicam II Paschae erit transferenda.

summary_en: In the introduction to the updated General Roman Calendar (1969-1989) the Congregation states that, although the Normae universales (n. 5) provide for solemnities falling on a Sunday of Advent, Lent or Easter to be anticipated to the Saturday, it considers it preferable to move the solemnities of St Joseph and of the Annunciation to the following Monday when they fall on a Sunday of Lent, provided it is not Holy Week, so as to allow a complete celebration and avoid uncertainty about the Saturday evening Mass; an unsigned editorial note with no protocol or date, followed by a table of occurrences for 1990-2008.
excerpt: Cependant, pour permettre une célébration complète de la solennité de Saint Joseph et de celle de l'Annonciation, et pour éviter toute incertitude sur la messe à célébrer le samedi soir, la Congrégation pour le Culte Divin et la Discipline des Sacrements estime préférable de renvoyer ces deux solennités au lendemain lundi, pourvu que ce ne soit pas pendant la Semaine Sainte.

Responsa ad dubia proposita, 'Quibus in diebus ecclesiam dedicare convenit?' (no protocol or date printed) — the 2000 dedication reply named in issue #986. A church is not dedicated on a day whose own mystery may not be passed over (the Paschal Triduum, Christmas, the Epiphany, the Ascension, Pentecost Sunday, Ash Wednesday, the weekdays of Holy Week, the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed; Ordo Dedicationis Ecclesiae n. 7), and it is inadvisable to choose as the day of dedication one on which a solemnity or feast of the Lord, of the Blessed Virgin or of a saint is permanently fixed, since the fixed celebration would then have to be omitted or transferred every year. Where the solemnity of the Title and the Anniversary of Dedication of one church would be united in a single celebration, the Table of Liturgical Days always gives the Anniversary of Dedication precedence over the Title, though both remain celebrations of their own particular character.
excerpt: Similes difficultates reperiuntur etiam quando desideratur unire in unam celebrationem sollemnitatem Tituli et illam Anniversarii Dedicationis cuiusdam Ecclesiae: secundum normas liturgicas et singulari quidem modo ad normam Tabulae dierum liturgicorum secundum ordinem praecedentiae praevalet semper sollemnitas diei Anniversarii Dedicationis super illam Tituli.

summary_en: Response of the Congregation to a dubium (no protocol or date printed): only one heavenly patron may be constituted, celebrated as a rule at the rank of feast (the Apostolic See may grant the rank of solemnity); two or more saints may be chosen together only if they are inscribed in the calendar under one celebration; a secondary patron is added only by rare indult and is celebrated at the rank of memorial; only saints, not blesseds, may be patrons without special indult.

summary_en: Extract published under the heading 'Responsa - Circa feste e pietà popolare' from the Congregation's letter answering an Italian bishop's questions on the link between liturgical discipline and popular festivals and processions (no date printed). A non-liturgical Marian title may not be celebrated with a grade or with liturgical texts at all, and cannot be kept on a Sunday of Easter, since the Sundays of Easter take precedence over every solemnity (Norme generali n. 5); the celebration of a city's principal patron or of another title keeps its own liturgical date, and only the devotional procession may be held on a nearby Sunday in Ordinary Time, that Sunday being celebrated with the Sunday's own texts, the competent authority weighing the criteria of Norme generali n. 58.
excerpt: Le Norme generali per l’Anno liturgico e il Calendario stabiliscono che le domeniche di Pasqua hanno la precedenza su tutte le solennità liturgiche (cf. n. 5). Nel caso, si tratta di “un titolo mariano non liturgico” e, dunque, neppure celebrabile con grado e con testi liturgici.
